newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia won't talk grain imports during U.S. visit.
newsitem.headline: Russia won't talk grain imports during U.S. visit.

text.p: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Zaveryukha does not intend to discuss U.S. grain imports when he visits Washington later this week, the official Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.

It quoted a member of Zaveryukha's team as saying Russia would import a small, unspecified amount of grain through commercial, not government, structures for its Far East, but discussions of U.S. imports were not on the agenda.

Zaveryukha, who is in charge of the harvest, travels with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to participate in two days of talks with U.S. officials, including Vice-President Al Gore, beginning Wednesday.

Tass said Zaveryukha would discuss land reform and development of agricultural trade ties at the talks, known as the Gore-Chernomyrdin Commission, or the U.S.-Russian Joint Commission on Economic and Technical Coooperation.
The talks are designed to foster investments and trade.
Tass quoted Zaveryukha as saying Russia's 1997 harvest was targeted at a net 70 million tonnes.
Output for 1996, the second poor showing in a row and one of the worst on record in three decades, was officially a net 69.3 million tonnes.
